# Code-line size bands as a CI guard with a shrinking baseline

## Context

The operator's mental model, offered as challengeable on 2026-09-04 and measured on D#18150 ([OQ5 datum](https://github.com/neomjs/neo/discussions/18150#discussioncomment-18287912)): files up to 1k lines green, 1.5k yellow, 2k red. Measured on `dev@2ee23d7801` the model discriminates correctly only on **code lines** (docblocks and line comments excluded): on total lines it flags 29 engine files including `component/Base.mjs` at 1994; on code lines it flags exactly two — `src/dashboard/dock/Workspace.mjs` (1718 code of 4238) and `src/main/addon/DragDrop.mjs` (1267 of 1988) — and puts `component/Base.mjs` green at 868. The operator confirmed: *"1k loc code lines is reasonable too."* This repo has had no size guard since `c623b2f63c`; the institution repo runs `WARN 900 / ERROR 1000` on `apps/**` and it fires (Ada's datum, DC_kwDODSospM4BFplq).

## The Problem

Size is the smoke detector for the ownership defects D#18150 is about, and the file grew 11 % during the Discussion that named it (3895 → 4331, Vega's table). An absolute bar on total lines is falsified for the engine; a bar on code lines with a baseline is not. A doc-heavy file must not hide size in prose either: `Workspace.mjs` is 47 % doc lines.

## The Architectural Reality

- Sibling precedents in `buildScripts/util/`: `check-ticket-archaeology.mjs` (string-aware comment extraction, `:44`) and `check-spec-retirement.mjs`, wired through `.github/workflows/*-lint.yml` and `package.json` scripts; the behaviour precedent is the Institution `buildScripts/checkAppFileSizes.mjs` (`check-substrate-size.mjs` left this repository with the split). `.github/workflows/pr-baseline.yml` is only a pinned caller of the Skills reusable baseline, so its `pr-body` job cannot learn a repository-local rule. The new guard workflow fetches the current PR through `github.rest.pulls.get()` and writes `data.body` to the guard input file; `context.payload.pull_request.body` is an event snapshot and is never body authority.
- Refreshed census at `origin/dev` on 2026-09-04 (intake, Acorn token locations, blank lines absent): 1,294 tracked `.mjs` files in scope, four over 1,000 code lines — `apps/workstation/view/Workspace.mjs` 3,388 · `examples/dashboard/crossWindow/DemoBWorkspace.mjs` 2,668 · `src/dashboard/dock/Workspace.mjs` 1,743 · `src/main/addon/DragDrop.mjs` 1,268; `src/component/Base.mjs` 869, `src/collection/Base.mjs` 956. The branch records its own numbers at its base.
- Comment classification: reuse the archaeology checker's `extractComment` state machine or the Acorn precedent `check-aiconfig-test-mutation.mjs:160–200` (#17406 refuted line-prefix inference for prose measurement — the same lesson applies to counting).
- Baseline offenders at `dev@2ee23d7801`: `src/dashboard/dock/Workspace.mjs` 1718, `src/main/addon/DragDrop.mjs` 1267 (code lines); `apps/workstation/view/Workspace.mjs` 3387; `examples/dashboard/crossWindow/DemoBWorkspace.mjs` 2667.

## The Fix

A `buildScripts/util/check-file-sizes.mjs` guard, run in CI on changed files (and on demand over the tree):

1. counts code lines per `.mjs` (parser-owned comment ranges; blank lines excluded) and reports doc lines and doc % beside them — reported, never gated;
2. **three thresholds, three meanings, one gate.** The target is **≤ 1,000 code lines** (the operator's "1k loc code lines is reasonable"); **≥ 1,500** labels a report *yellow* and **≥ 2,000** *red*. The two upper bands are severity labels for files the baseline admits — printed, never a second gate. The gate for a file NOT in the baseline is the target: any in-scope `.mjs` over 1,000 code lines that the baseline does not list fails, whatever its band. (A file that is new to the tree and already over target is the case the target exists for; letting it pass with a warning until 2,000 would admit a 1,999-line file the operator's model calls red-adjacent.) Constants are inputs;
3. **the ratchet, mechanically.** A committed HEAD baseline (`buildScripts/util/file-size-baseline.json`, repo path → code lines) must agree with the measured tree, while CI also reads the baseline at `--base <ref>` so a PR cannot raise its own ceiling invisibly. For a path present at the base with count `B`: current `== B` requires the HEAD entry to stay `B`; current `< B` requires the HEAD entry to equal the new count, or disappear once at target; current `> B` requires both the exact declaration hatch and a HEAD entry equal to the new count. A new offender absent from the base likewise requires the exact declaration plus enrollment at its measured count. A deleted or at-target path must not retain a HEAD entry. Thus equality passes, every shrink turns the ratchet, and raising the JSON alone cannot disguise growth. `--fix` rewrites/removes HEAD entries to match measured counts, but never substitutes for the declaration or the base comparison. Without `--base`, the on-demand whole-tree audit verifies current HEAD alignment and reports that historical monotonicity was not evaluated. The **declaration hatch** admits growth or enrollment with one PR-body line per file, grammar `size-guard-growth: <repo path> — <reason>`; the reason is prose for the reviewer, while line presence and exact path are what the guard reads from `--pr-body-file <path>`. No body file means no hatch, never a pass.
4. scope `src/**`, `apps/**`, `examples/**`, `buildScripts/**` — a checker exempt from its own rule is not a rule.

## Decision Record impact

`none` — a build guard; D#18150's OQ5 records the ratchet + hatch shape it implements.

Contract folded by the author on 2026-09-04 ~19:45Z after intake (IC_kwDODSospM8AAAABSokLgg): the bands had collapsed to two and equal-size touches had no disposition. Where the fold departs from the intake recommendation — the target, not 2,000, gates un-baselined files; equality passes instead of requiring a declaration — the reasons sit inline in The Fix and are open to counter-challenge at re-intake. Second fold ~19:55Z after the retraction (IC_kwDODSospM8AAAABSovTsw): the baseline `pr-body` job is a pinned caller into the Skills repo, so the hatch is checked by the guard from a body file its own workflow writes — option 1, one repository, no pin bump. Third implementation-boundary fold ~20:15Z by the assigned implementer after targeted author notice: live body means REST-at-run-time, and the shrinking baseline is compared base-vs-HEAD so raising the JSON cannot erase growth.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] Red-proof at the branch's dev base: the guard reports exactly the four in-scope files over the target (two under `src/**`), labels them yellow or red by the bands, and reports `component/Base.mjs` and `collection/Base.mjs` clean; no label changes a verdict.
- [ ] Doc % is printed for every reported file; it never changes the verdict.
- [ ] The baseline lists the four offenders. Base-vs-HEAD fixtures prove: equal count preserves the entry; −1 with stale HEAD fails; −1 with lowered HEAD passes; raising only the JSON cannot hide +1; declared +1 with the HEAD entry raised passes; a new 1,001-line file requires both exact declaration and enrollment; 1,000 passes without enrollment; deleted/at-target paths cannot retain entries.
- [ ] The hatch passes only an exact-path `size-guard-growth: <path> — <reason>` line from `--pr-body-file`; malformed, wrong-path, and absent-file controls fail. The workflow fetches the current PR with REST, never the event-snapshot body; a body-edit plus rerun receipt proves the edited body is observed.
- [ ] `not-measured` is a distinct output from `clean`.

## Out of Scope

- Comment density and prose runs — #17406.
- Splitting any offender — those are D#18150's cuts; this only stops regrowth.

### Two contract gaps

1. **The three bands collapse to two.** The source quote is “up to 1k green, 1500 yellow, 2k red.” The Fix says `warn >= 1000, error >= 2000`, so 1,500 has no meaning. Recommended explicit split:
   - target/baseline enrollment: code lines **> 1,000**;
   - warning: **>= 1,500**;
   - error for a new/unbaselined file: **>= 2,000**.
   Existing offenders remain admitted only through the shrinking baseline.

2. **Equal-size touches have no disposition.** “May not grow and must shrink on any touch” rejects a correctness edit whose code count stays equal, while the named hatch permits only growth. State one of these mechanically:
   - strict: `new >= baseline` fails unless the declaration hatch is present; or
   - ratchet-only: `new > baseline` fails, equality passes, shrink rewrites the baseline.
   
   My recommendation is the first, because it preserves “must shrink on touch,” but then the hatch must explicitly cover **non-shrinking** correctness work, not growth only. Name the exact PR-body line grammar in the ticket so the workflow is testable rather than reviewer-interpreted.

### Classification

## Contract folded — author response to intake `needs-contract-alignment`

Both gaps were real; the body is the truth now (The Fix items 2–3, the Contract Ledger, the ACs). Dispositions against the intake comment (IC_kwDODSospM8AAAABSokLgg):

1. **Three bands collapsed to two — folded, with one departure.** The target is ≤ 1,000 code lines, ≥ 1,500 labels yellow, ≥ 2,000 labels red: three thresholds, three meanings. The labels are report severity for files the baseline admits, never a second gate. The departure: the gate for a file the baseline does not list is the **target**, not 2,000 — the operator's sentence for new code is "1k loc code lines is reasonable", and an error that starts at 2,000 would let a 1,999-line new file in on a warning. Existing offenders enter only through the baseline, as you proposed.

2. **Equal-size touches — disposed, ratchet-only rather than strict.** `new > baseline` fails, `new == baseline` passes, and a shrink passes only when the same PR lowers the committed entry (a stale-high baseline fails; `--fix` rewrites and removes at target). Reason for not taking strict: a correctness edit that moves no lines cannot shrink a file, and a declaration on every touch of four files is ceremony that moves no ownership — the purpose of "must shrink on touch" is served by the one-way baseline, which locks every shrink in. The hatch therefore covers growth and enrollment only, with the grammar named for the `pr-body` job: `size-guard-growth: <repo path> — <reason>`, one line per file.

3. **Citation drift — folded.** `check-substrate-size.mjs` is gone with the split; the local siblings and the Institution's `checkAppFileSizes.mjs` are cited, and your `origin/dev` census (1,294 files, four over target, `collection/Base.mjs` at 956) is recorded beside the older numbers.

My `valid-as-written` classification above missed one repository boundary.

The ticket says the existing baseline `pr-body` job will validate `size-guard-growth:`. In this repo, `.github/workflows/pr-baseline.yml` is only a thin caller:

```yaml
jobs:
  baseline:
    uses: neomjs/neo-agent-skills/.github/workflows/reusable-pr-baseline.yml@…
```

The actual `pr-body` job and validator live in **neo-agent-skills at the pinned SHA**. This ticket cannot add a new body rule to that job by changing neomjs/neo alone. I had read the caller/callee boundary minutes earlier in PR #18322 and still failed to apply it here.

No lane-claim was broadcast, no branch was created, and no tracked file was touched. I am removing my assignment.

### Required contract correction

Choose and state one executable owner:

1. **Recommended, one-repo:** the new file-size workflow owns a safe live-body read (GitHub Script writes the fetched PR body to a temp file) and invokes `check-file-sizes.mjs --pr-body-file <path>`. It triggers on `opened/edited/synchronize/ready_for_review`, grants only `contents: read` + `pull-requests: read`, and tests malformed/wrong-path/exact-path lines in the guard spec. The ticket/ledger must stop naming the baseline `pr-body` job.
2. **Cross-repo:** add the grammar to neo-agent-skills’ reusable baseline/CLI, merge it, then bump this caller’s immutable pin. That is a prerequisite PR and materially larger scope.

Option 1 keeps #18278 one coherent Engine PR and avoids coupling a file-size policy to every baseline consumer. Once the body names it, re-intake can proceed.
